newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lukoil expands on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lukoil expands on foreign markets.

text.p: Russia's largest oil company Lukoil Thursday launched a programme for foreign investors to trade preferred shares abroad and announced major plans for new international issues.

Traders began selling American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), each representing two underlying Lukoil preferred shares, after the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved them late Wednesday, the company said.
Preferred share prices of Lukoil, which account for about one-fifth of the Russian equity market's capitalisation, jumped to $12.60 at the close in Moscow Thursday from $11.75 at Wednesday's close.
The head of Lukoil's securities department said the company intended to float another 15 percent of company equity on foreign markets by the end of the year.

"The larger the market, the larger the circle of investors," said Lukoil Vice-President Leonid Fedun, who said the company planned to sell the government-owned stake as a special class of more prominent ADRs.

"I'm not looking for a strategic investor -- I'm looking for financial investors," Fedun said, explaining Lukoil was happy with its Western partner Atlantic Richfield Co. and wanted more Russian portfolio investors -- and funds.
"We have waited four years," Fedun said of the plan to issue the 15 percent stake as level-three ADRs.
These ADRs require a company to present three years of international-standard accounts and allows companies to raise new capital.
"We think we will get the best price in 1997," he said.

Fedun said that net profits, to Russian accounting standards, which are not prepared for investment decision-making, could decline in 1997 from 1996's more than 3.7 trillion rubles ($660 million), due to capital spending.

But he said oil production had risen 3 percent in January over a year earlier, and Lukoil still expected 1997 production to rise to 59.7 million metric tons (439 million barrels) from 58.3 million in 1996 (428 million barrels).

Lukoil also plans a level-one global depository receipt listing in London by April and has plans, which Fedun said are awaiting government approval, to issue options this year for just under 5 percent of shares.

The level-one preferred share ADRs introduced Thursday, as well as level-one ADRs representing ordinary shares that are listed in Berlin, Frankfurt and on the Nasdaq bulletin board, represent existing shares of OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya Lukoil.
Lukoil has already had talks with Japanese firms about participating in the 15 percent stake sale, Fedun said, though he declined to give details.
By year end, the Russian government will be left with only 6.6 percent of Lukoil, less than the 7.99 percent owned by Atlantic Richfield.
